# HelioField

> HelioField shows the Sun's coronal magnetic field in 3D for any date since 2010-05-01: potential-field source-surface (PFSS) field lines from NSO/GONG and SDO/HMI magnetograms, the source surface and its neutral line, the heliospheric current sheet, and the magnetic connection of planets and spacecraft (Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, STEREO, BepiColombo, the L1 fleet) to their source regions on the Sun, with expansion factor, distance to the coronal-hole boundary and a WSA-type wind-speed estimate. Optional Schatten current-sheet (SCS) model out to 21.5 solar radii. Free, open source (MIT), no account or key.

Site: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/
Machine-readable parameters: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/api.json
Guide (methods, validation, limitations): https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/guide.html
Source: https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofield · Cite: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23487231

## How an agent can use it

There are two ways to show a user the 3D corona without writing a model:

1. **Give a link, or embed it (needs a browser).** Every view is a URL. Build one from the parameters below and give it to the user, put it in an iframe, or open it in a browser tool and take a screenshot. The page computes any date in the browser (a few seconds; WebGL needed). For a screenshot, add `embed=1` so a past date computes without a confirmation dialog, and wait until the field lines appear.
2. **Make images with Python (no browser).** Download the HelioField scripts and run one command. It fetches the same inputs as the page, solves the field and writes PNG and PDF figures plus a NetCDF results file.

```bash
pip install numpy scipy matplotlib
base=https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/download
for f in heliofield_io.py heliofield_update.py compute_corona.py plot_3d.py plot_surface.py requirements.txt requirements-tested.txt; do curl -sO "$base/$f"; done
python compute_corona.py --date 2014-03-12 --plot --view earth            # PFSS
python compute_corona.py --date 2020-05-08 --scs 21.5 --plot --view fleet # PFSS + current-sheet model
```

Outputs, in the working directory:
- `heliofield_model-<date>_computed-<today>_<pfss|scs>_3d.png` and `.pdf`: the 3D view;
- `..._surface.png` and `.pdf`: three surface maps (photospheric B_r, source-surface B_r with the neutral line, open-field footprints with spacecraft footpoints);
- `....nc` and `..._header.json`: the results.

Options:
- `--rss 1.5..3.5`: source-surface height;
- `--scs 5|10|21.5`: couple the current-sheet model out to that radius;
- `--view home|earth|north|fleet`: the camera;
- `--theme light|dark`;
- `--v <km/s>`: the wind speed used for the spacecraft connections.

`python plot_3d.py FILE.nc --lon L --lat B --dist D` sets the camera freely. PFSS takes a few seconds and SCS 10–20 s. The scripts are tested every month against the newest NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib, and update themselves if they fail.

## URL recipes

- Today's corona from Earth: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=latest&view=earth
- A past date from Earth: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=2014-03-12&view=earth
- Whole fleet with its magnetic connections: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=latest&view=fleet
- Heliospheric current sheet out to 1 au at true scale: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=latest&view=fleet&layers=photo,hcs,fleet,spiral&scale=true&rmax=1.2
- Open field extended into the heliosphere: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=latest&layers=photo,closed,open,ext,pil,fleet,spiral
- Coronal holes (open-field footprints): https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=latest&layers=photo,foot,open,pil&view=earth
- PFSS + Schatten current sheet out to 21.5 R_sun, past date: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=2020-05-08&scs=21.5&view=fleet&layers=photo,closed,open,pil,hcs,fleet,spiral
- Lower source surface (2.0 R_sun), past date: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=2014-03-12&rss=2&view=earth
- Clean embed for another page: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/?date=latest&view=earth&embed=1&controls=0&theme=light
- The same date on HelioFleet (spacecraft positions, instrument fields, observations): https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/?t=YYYY-MM-DDT12:00Z&spirals=1&wind=V, and its sky view from a spacecraft: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofleet/sky.html?t=YYYY-MM-DDT12:00Z&obs=solo

## Connectivity page

`https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/connect.html?date=YYYY-MM-DD` covers the in-situ spacecraft (Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, BepiColombo, STEREO-A, Earth/L1). It shows, for each:
- its magnetic footpoint (ballistic Parker spiral, then PFSS or PFSS + SCS field line);
- the travel time and the **source time** (when the plasma it measures left the Sun);
- f_s, DCHB and the WSA-type speed;
- the **predicted IMF polarity** (outward or inward), with the share of the footpoint spread that agrees and the angle to the current sheet;
- the predicted polarity day by day over a rotation (sector structure);
- the HelioFleet observations (IRIS, Hinode/EIS, DKIST, Solar Orbiter EUI-HRI, PHI-HRT, SPICE) whose field contains or lies within 5° of the footpoint during the source-time window, with data links;
- the model current sheet in coronagraph fields (LASCO, COR1/COR2, Metis, WISPR, SoloHI, VELC, CCOR, ASPIICS, PUNCH NFI).

Parameters:
- `date`;
- `scs` (`5`, `10` or `21.5`);
- `rss`;
- `v`;
- `conn=sc`;
- `focus` (`psp`, `solo`, `bepi`, `sta`, `stb` or `earth`);
- `ins` (instrument id);
- `bg=open`;
- `theme`.

Examples:
- https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/connect.html?date=2025-03-22
- https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/connect.html?date=2025-03-22&scs=21.5&focus=solo&ins=metis

## Space-weather page

`https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/spaceweather.html?date=YYYY-MM-DD` turns one day's product into space-weather indicators (dates with a daily product only; default: the latest). It shows:
- an assessment in words, and tiles: model wind speed at Earth, peak in the next 7 days, magnetic sector and next sector boundary, Russell-McPherron season, interplanetary field strength from open flux, coronal holes facing Earth, sector bias at Earth's latitude (Rosenberg-Coleman), DONKI event counts;
- the solar-wind outlook at Earth, 13 days back to 14 days ahead: WSA-type speeds on the source surface carried to 1 au with the HUX kinematic model, the sector, and which days rest on far-side data;
- coronal holes within 35 degrees of the equator, with central-meridian passage and fast-wind arrival windows;
- the southward share of the Parker-spiral field (GSM) through the year for both sectors;
- upstream lead times of Parker Solar Probe, Solar Orbiter, STEREO-A and BepiColombo relative to Earth;
- footpoints for particle-event connectivity, and the angular distance of DONKI flares (M5+) from each;
- DONKI CMEs (1000 km/s+) with cone geometry and drag-based arrival estimates, and G3+ storms;
- solar-cycle context from the rotation series;
- the model against measurement: each day's predictions (same day to 7 days ahead) next to the daily-mean solar wind measured at L1, with error, bias, correlation and sector hit rate per lead time.

It describes the ambient wind only, uses illustrative WSA coefficients, and is not an official forecast (that is NOAA SWPC). Share buttons for X, Facebook, LinkedIn, Bluesky, Reddit, WhatsApp and email.

Each recorded day also has a share card, https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/sw/YYYY-MM-DD.png (1200 x 630: status, wind at Earth, 7-day peak, sector, outlook), and a share page, https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/sw/YYYY-MM-DD.html, which carries the card in its preview tags and redirects to the assessment. The newest card is https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/sw/latest.png. Each row of `data/spaceweather/daily.json` also has `model.level`: `good`, `watch`, `high` or `severe`.

Parameters:
- `date`;
- `bg=open` (coronal-hole map instead of source-surface speed);
- `lead` (`0`, `1`, `3`, `5` or `7` days: which predictions to compare with measurements; default 1);
- `embed=1` (the status, four headline tiles and the wind outlook alone, for an iframe; with `theme`);
- `theme`.

Example: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/spaceweather.html?date=2026-11-02

## Observations page

`https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/observations.html?date=YYYY-MM-DD` shows, for every day of the last 60 and one day per Carrington rotation back to May 2010, the images (the frame nearest the map time) from SDO/AIA (94, 131, 171, 193, 211, 304, 335, 1600 A) and HMI, SOHO/LASCO C2 and C3, STEREO-A/EUVI and Solar Orbiter/EUI (174, 304 A) and PHI, with the model's field lines drawn from each spacecraft's own position. Images come from the companion repository https://github.com/sr-dash/heliofield-imagery (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23935774; data: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield-imagery/index.json and days/<date>/index.json). Each panel compares a standard and an enhanced rendering (WOW for disk images, NRGF for LASCO, whose standard rendering is the ratio to a four-week minimum background).

Parameters:
- `date`;
- `view` (`std`, `cmp` or `enh`: where every panel's slider starts; default `cmp`);
- `scs` (`0`: PFSS from the HMI rotation map; `5`, `10` or `21.5`: PFSS + Schatten current sheet to that radius from the HMI rotation map; omitted: the day's PFSS, or the HMI rotation map on days before the daily products);
- `v` (wind speed for the spirals beyond the model: 300 to 700 km/s);
- `closed=0`, `open=0`, `sheet=0`, `grid=0` (hide closed lines, open lines, the current sheet, the grid and compass);
- `alpha` (line opacity, 0 to 100) and `width` (line width, 0.3 to 4 times the default);
- `imagery` (another base URL for the images);
- `embed=1` (four panels in a 2 x 2 grid, for an iframe; a click opens the full page) and `panels` (with `embed`: comma list of panel ids, `a|b` taking the first present; default `aia193,lasco_c2,eui174|euvi_a,hmi|phi`);
- `theme`.

Example: https://sr-dash.github.io/heliofield/observations.html?date=2026-11-02&view=enh

## URL parameters

- `date`: YYYY-MM-DD from 2010-05-01, or `latest` (default). Recent days use daily server products (GONG, or the HMI fallback). Other days are computed in the browser from the SDO/HMI Carrington-rotation map covering the date. On the full page, a computed date first shows a dialog: click **Compute**, then wait a few seconds. With `embed=1` it computes without asking, which suits browser tools.
- `view`: `earth` (as seen from Earth), `north` (over the north pole) or `fleet` (zoomed out to all spacecraft). Without it, an oblique view.
- `cam`: `lon,lat,dist`, a fixed camera (Carrington longitude and latitude in degrees, distance in display units). Overrides `view`.
- `layers`: comma list from `photo` (surface B_r), `foot` (open-field footprints), `closed`, `open` (field lines), `ext` (open lines continued into the heliosphere), `ss` (source-surface B_r), `pil` (neutral line), `hcs` (current sheet), `fleet` (planets and spacecraft), `spiral` (connections to the Sun), `cloud` (footpoint spread). Default: `photo,closed,open,pil,fleet,spiral`.
- `v`: solar-wind speed for the spirals and connections: 300, 400 (default), 500, 600, 700 or 800 km/s.
- `conn`: `sc` lets each spacecraft connect at its own footpoint's estimated speed.
- `ext`: `radial` continues open lines straight out instead of as Parker spirals.
- `rmax`: how far the current sheet and extended lines reach, 0.1–1.8 au (default 1.2).
- `scale`: `true` for true distances (default: log distances beyond the source surface).
- `lines`: number of field lines drawn (default 250, up to about 740).
- `ss`: source-surface opacity, 0–1.
- `rss`: source-surface height, 1.5–3.5 R_sun (default 2.5). Computed dates only.
- `scs`: `5`, `10` or `21.5` couples the Schatten current-sheet model out to that radius. Computed dates only.
- `rotate`: `1` rotates slowly.
- `theme`: `dark` or `light`.
- `embed`: `1` gives the embedded layout. With it, `controls=0` hides the date bar, `panel=0|1` closes or opens the menu, and `series=0|1` hides or shows the solar-cycle panel.

An embedded page can also be driven with postMessage. Send `{type: "heliofield:set", date, v, rss, scs, view, layers, conn}`. The page answers `{type: "heliofield:state", date, v, rss, scs, source, computed, obstime}`.

## Data (JSON and binary, CORS-free static files on the site)

- `data/index.json`: dates with daily products (`dates`, `updated`).
- `data/<date>/meta.json`: a daily product. It holds:
  - `model`, `source`, `L0`, `B0` and `open_flux_Mx`;
  - `hcs`: source-surface neutral lines as flat `[lon, lat, ...]` lists;
  - `fleet`: each body's Carrington `lon`, `lat`, `r` in au;
  - `connect`: per body and speed, the source-surface point `ss`, the footpoint `foot`, `fs`, `dchb` and `vwsa`;
  - `vgrid`;
  - `wsa`: the speed map's file and range.
- `data/<date>/wsa.png`: WSA-type speed traced from every 1-degree cell of the source surface, 360 x 180 grey PNG, north row first; 0 no value, 1-255 linear over `wsa.vmin`-`wsa.vmax` km/s.
- `data/spaceweather/daily.json`: the space-weather time series, one row per day: `model` (from that day's product: `v`, `sector`, `next_boundary`, `peak7`, `imf_nT`, `open_flux`, `rm`, `rc_away`, `holes_facing`, and `fc_v`/`fc_b`, the predicted daily-mean speed and sector at Earth for UTC days -1 to +7) and `measured` (daily means at L1: `v`, `v_min`, `v_max`, `b`, `bz`, `away`, `n`, `kp_max`, `dst_min`, `src` = `OMNI` or `SWPC RTSW`). Units in `units`.
- `data/spaceweather/inputs/<year>.json`: per day, the WSA inputs `fs` and `dchb` and the source-surface field sign `b` along Earth's latitude (360 longitudes from 0.5 deg), with `t0`, `L0`, `lat`, `r`, `rss`, for recalibrating the speed formula (`scripts/calibrate_wsa.py`).
- `data/history/index.json`: the archive of HMI rotation maps (`rotations`: `cr`, `start`, `stop`, `file`; `shape`; `scale_G`). Each `data/history/cr/<CR>.bin.gz` is gzipped int16 × 0.1 G, 180 × 360, rows uniform in sin(latitude) from the south, column j at Carrington longitude j + 0.5°.
- `data/history/fleet/<year>.json`: daily Carrington positions at 12:00 UTC, and Earth's L0, B0 and Carrington rotation.
- `data/series/rotations.json`: per Carrington rotation since 2010: open flux, open area, current-sheet tilt (north and south) and polar field.

## Limits to tell users

- PFSS is a current-free model. It cannot show sheared or erupting fields, and its open flux is typically about half of what is measured in situ.
- A computed date uses a Carrington-rotation map built over about 27 days, so it shows the field around that date.
- The browser smooths the map (FWHM 3.8°). The daily products use the full map.
- Wind speeds are indicative; the coefficients are not tuned.
- Results are model output, not observations. Cite HelioField and the magnetogram (NSO/GONG or SDO/HMI).
